steps.text: Place the chipotle peppers, garlic, cayenne pepper, paprika, black pepper, cumin, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, honey, vinegar, and olive oil into a blender. Puree until no pieces of garlic remain. Pour 1/4 of the marinade into a small dish and set aside. Rub a pinch of kosher salt into each chicken drumstick and place into a resealable plastic bag. Pour in the marinade, shake, and seal. Marinade at least 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove the chicken from the marinade and shake off excess. Discard the remaining marinade.

Cook the chicken legs on the preheated grill until no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, about 8 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted near the bone should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Once the legs are completely cooked, baste well with the remaining marinade, cover the grill, and cook and additional 2 minutes per side to glaze.

raw_recipe.headline: Chipotle Marinated Grilled Chicken
raw_recipe.description: The chipotle marinade used on this chicken is very spicy by itself, but when used on meats, it leaves only a little kick without being overpowering.

review.reviewBody: This was a pretty good marinade. I think the longer you marinate, the better. I used this on boneless chicken breasts, put everything into a ziploc bag and let it marinate for 4 hours. Next time I would let it go longer. The honey gave it a nice sweetness and it wasn't overly spicy.

Very good, I followed recipe except I baked it instead of grilling it. Baked at 350 for 40 minutes on a broiler pan, then switched it to a shallow dish and poured extra sauce over it( I made two seperate batches of the marinade). I used more chipotle peppers than just three ( the whole can between the two batches of sauce that I made) because I love Spicy. I was very happy with the way the chicken turned out!!! Thank you!!!

I made this but skipped the blender. just whisked it all together then let it sit with the chicken for 4 hours.

the left over marinade was heated up on the stove top and used as a glaze.

apple wood chips on the grill just added to the rich smokey flavor.

Hey all, this is my recipe. Thanks for the compliments. To clarify, this was intended for whole legs, not drubsticks, that's why it makes so much marinade. But of course, you can use it on anything. You'd probably be safe halving everything though if you're cooking for 4. Making tonight for company :)

Wow, this was a crowed pleaser. I quadrupled the recipe but only used 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and it was the perfect blend of sweet and spicy. I marinated drumsticks and thighs overnight and grilled them on medium low for about 45 minutes. I will make this again!

I used this as a marinade for diced chicken breasts, and cooked them on my stove top and used it for fajitas! I didn't have any chipotle peppers, so I used chipotle flakes, and garlic powder rather than cloves. I cut the balsamic vinegar in half, and that was well more than enough. Awesome for chicken that's going in fajitas and quesadillas!

This was a great recipe. I doubled everything except the cayenne pepper and it had the perfect amount of heat. I used BLSLCB cutlets which marinated for about 30 hours. Very flavorful, delicious recipe! Thanks for sharing, PhillyKev!

Amazing, best marinade I've ever made. I did not have any balsamic vinegar, so I added extra lime juice which was perfect for my mexican chicken fajitas (I used a mix of breast & thighs). I also did not put the cayenne pepper, and it was perfectly spicy from the chipotles for me. I used the extra on some pork chops and grilled them, and they were amazing too. I feel like this marinade will work on any meat! I marinated my meat both times for almost 24 hours.

This was really good. I used boneless skinless breasts & I also added just a little more honey to the marinade but those were the only changes. I also sauteed some zuchinni and red peppers and finished them with a raspberry chipotle sauce (from Sam's). I plated the veggies and then placed the chicken on top and Mmmm was it ever a flavor sensation! Served with oven baked sweet potato fries with a chipotle sour cream sauce. Thanks so much for sharing.

this came out very tasty with the following modifications.. i had no chipotle peppers, only sauce so i used 3 T of it.. doubled the paprika, black paper, and cumin.. left out the honey and completely forgot the oil.. added about 1 tsp of salt to the marinade and it was enough for 4 chicken quarters.. ty for the start of a very delicious dish
Used this marinade for shrimp skewers. Marinated for about three hours and then thru on the grill for a couple minutes on each side. Outstanding!

This was excellent! There is a lot of different flavors going on but they all come together nicely. Not sure about boneless drumsticks though? I've never seen them. I also chose to leave the skin on to get a good crisp.
Yummy
Perfect the way it is. Im cooking for 4 so the amount is perfect.
Not sure why this wasn’t more successful. Actually marinated overnight so should have been even more flavorful. Was ok but not not great. I used boneless chicken breast instead. Oh well.
I used boneless, skinless thighs instead of drumsticks but did everything else the same. I marinated it over night and the chicken was delicious and I have enough leftover for lunch tomorrow! Win!!!
I used apple cider vinegar and red pepper instead of cayenne!
Very good. I would definitely make it again
The flavors do not come together for me.
This was great! Thank you for the recipe!
